info.title: DomScan
info.description:
DomScan is a domain intelligence API providing domain analysis tools.

**Core Features:**
- Domain Availability: Check single or bulk domains using RDAP with 1,100+ TLDs supported
- Domain Intelligence: AI suggestions, valuations, health checks, typosquatting detection
- OSINT Tools: DNS lookup, WHOIS/RDAP, SSL certificates, subdomain discovery, IP geolocation, tech stack detection
- Social & Branding: Social handle checker, brand name scoring
- Phone Intelligence: Privacy-first phone number validation, normalization, and classification
- Pricing: Scheduled standard-TLD tables from verified official registrar sources, plus separate credential-backed exact-domain quotes
- Watchlist: Domain monitoring for expiration and availability alerts

**Authentication:**
Most API endpoints require authentication. Pass your API key via the x-api-key header or Authorization: Bearer header. Operations marked with an empty security requirement are intentionally public, including API specifications and selected catalog endpoints. Get your free API key at https://domscan.net/dashboard. Logged-in users on domscan.net tools pages are authenticated automatically via session cookie.

**Rate Limits:**
Free accounts can sustain 120 requests per minute per account, with a burst capacity of 60. All API keys and dashboard sessions belonging to the same free account share this budget.

Bulk endpoints have an additional free-tier budget of 20 HTTP requests per minute per account across all bulk endpoints. Free-tier bulk traffic is also capped at 100 requests per minute per IPv4 address or IPv6 /56 network. Platform-wide edge protections still apply to every tier.

Paid accounts can sustain 600 requests per minute, with a burst capacity of 120, shared by every API key and dashboard session of the account. Paid accounts do not receive the additional free-tier bulk budget.

Scope: RapidAPI subscribers are counted per subscriber. (scope=rapidapi-customer) Zyla subscribers are counted per subscriber when the gateway identifies them, (scope=zyla-customer) and as one shared gateway budget when it does not. (scope=zyla-gateway) Other authenticated requests are counted per account: every API key and dashboard session of the account shares one budget. (scope=account) A key that is not linked to an account is counted on its own. (scope=api-key) Unauthenticated requests to public endpoints are counted per client IP address (scope unknown when the address cannot be determined, as one shared budget). (scope=ip)

Every authenticated response, success or error, includes X-RateLimit-Plan, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and X-RateLimit-Policy. X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining describe the immediate burst bucket; X-RateLimit-Reset is the Unix time in seconds when that bucket is full again; X-RateLimit-Policy also states the sustained per-minute rate, scope, and any free bulk limits. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Retry only after the indicated delay.

**Credits System:**
API calls consume credits based on endpoint complexity. Sign up for free to receive 10,000 credits monthly.
- 1 credit: Status checks, DNS lookups, tool builders
- 2-5 credits: Health checks, valuations, OSINT tools
- Bulk endpoints: standard per-item rate for batching multiple items into fewer HTTP requests.
- 6-25 credits: Recipe compound operations

When credits reach zero, the API returns HTTP 402 with credits_remaining, credits_required, and a purchase_url. API responses include X-Credits-Requested, X-Credits-Charged, and X-Credits-Refunded. X-Credits-Charged is the net charge after any refund made during the request. Authenticated responses also include X-Credits-Remaining whenever the balance is known without an extra lookup. Free credits refresh monthly on the account's signup anniversary.

POST /v1/estimate returns the credits a request would charge without running it, at no cost. Bulk, compare, recipe and pricing endpoints also accept dry_run=true, which returns the same estimate for the request as sent, with HTTP 200 and no charge.

**Idempotency:**
Every POST that charges credits accepts an optional Idempotency-Key header (printable ASCII, 1 to 255 characters). Retrying with the same key, the same API key and the same request within 24 hours returns the stored response with Idempotent-Replayed: true and charges nothing again. Reusing a key for a different request returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a retry that arrives while the first request is still running returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS. Only responses that succeeded or kept a charge, with a body up to 1 MiB, are stored; any other response releases the key, so the retry runs again. Job and batch creation endpoints keep their own Idempotency-Key rules. Requests without the header behave exactly as before.

**Error Handling:**
Every API error uses one canonical JSON shape: an error object with code, message, type, status, retryable, request_id, and docs_url, plus optional suggestion, details, and retry_after. request_id always equals the X-Request-Id response header. Codes are stable upper-case strings and are never renamed; the full catalog with HTTP status, type, and retryability is published as x-domscan-error-codes (RATE_LIMITED is canonical and RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED is an accepted alias). Endpoint-specific fields that existed before, such as credits_remaining, purchase_url, login_url, success, or meta, are kept during the compatibility period, so existing clients keep working. Unknown /v1 paths return 404 NOT_FOUND and unsupported methods return 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED with an Allow header. Handle HTTP 200, 201, 400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 405, 409, 410, 422, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 in your client. Retry only when retryable is true, after retry_after or Retry-After when present.

general.scope: API key for key-authenticated requests; IP for browser sessions

x-domscan-response-metadata.compatibility: additive response headers; established JSON success bodies are unchanged

headers.X-Request-Id: Unique request identifier for logs and support
headers.X-Credits-Charged: Credits retained after settlement, net of any refund in the request
headers.X-Credits-Remaining: Authenticated account balance after the request; omitted when it is not known without an extra lookup
headers.X-Data-Freshness: fresh, cached, stale, mixed, or unknown
headers.X-RateLimit-Reset: Unix time in seconds when the burst capacity is full again
headers.X-RateLimit-Plan: Active plan, or not_applicable before authentication
headers.Idempotent-Replayed: true when the response is a stored Idempotency-Key replay

x-domscan-response-metadata.mcp: POST /mcp responses carry X-Credits-Charged (summed over a JSON-RPC batch, which only protocols before 2025-06-18 accept, at most 20 messages) and X-Credits-Remaining when known. MCP tool calls do not use the REST burst bucket, so X-RateLimit headers are not sent there.

get.description: Query the DomScan WHOIS observation log. A qualifying fresh, successful RDAP-backed GET /v1/whois or /v2/whois lookup can record at most one normalized snapshot per domain per UTC day. Cached responses, bulk lookups, history reads, and traditional WHOIS-only fallbacks do not add snapshots. post.summary: Validate and normalize a phone number
post.description:
Validate one phone number against maintained international numbering-plan metadata and offline public-allocation data.

The endpoint accepts international numbers, national numbers with a two-letter default_country, extensions, Unicode digits, vanity numbers, short numbers with country context, and RFC 3966 tel: URIs. Parsing is strict, so unrelated text surrounding a number is rejected rather than silently extracted. Optional dialing_from_country adds caller-relative dialing formats, while language selects the language used for offline location and carrier labels.

The stable validation fields include E.164, international, national, and RFC 3966 formats, country or region, calling code, possible regions, number type, extension, country-match intelligence, and a decision-oriented status. The additive intelligence object can include a country-specific coverage level, numbering-plan location, possible time zones, original prefix carrier, regional portability support, dialing guidance, short-number signals, service classification, official allocation records, source provenance, and explicit accuracy warnings. United States results can match daily NANPA NPA-NXX central office code records. Canadian results can match nightly CNA/CNAC NPA-NXX status records. These sources describe prefix status and the original code holder, not the current carrier of a ported individual number.

**Privacy and scope:** The submitted number is checked using offline metadata and downloaded regulator snapshots. Customer lookups make zero paid or per-number third-party requests and the number is not persisted. A valid result means the number matches a current numbering-plan pattern. Location is a numbering-plan description, carrier is the original prefix carrier, and regulator data describes an allocated range. None proves that the individual number is assigned, active, reachable, owned by a particular subscriber, or currently served by any carrier.

**Credits:** 1 credit per number.
